subject: Renewal & capacity uplift — redlines and path to sign
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@hexatek.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@hexatek.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & capacity uplift — redlines and path to sign

Hi Sophie / Procurement,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment on the target start of the renewed term (Oct 1) and the capacity uplift (+300k tokens/month). Attached are the two items we discussed: a marked MSA with the limited term changes we proposed, and an order form that reflects the new seat/capacity counts plus proration through year-end.

Key asks from our side so we can move to signature this week:
- Confirm 24-month term (started Oct 1) versus the 12-month option; the MSA currently shows a 24-month term line item we put in red.
- Confirm whether HexaTek needs the higher retention (12 months) for logs — if so we need to add the Exhibit F language and there may be a small fee.
- Accept the proration approach on the order form: we prorate the first month for the capacity uplift and apply monthly thereafter.

Ben & Logan — please see the two highlighted clauses in the MSA where HexaTek asked for an explicit SLA credit formula. We propose keeping the SLA section unchanged and adding the credit mechanics to Exhibit C (see page 7 of the redline).

Sophie — once you confirm the term and retention preference I can route the updated docs to Legal Ops and email you a DocuSign packet for signature. If Procurement wants to push back on indemnity carveouts, flag names and I’ll coordinate counsel.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: HexaTek_MSA_redline_v2.docx (docx, 245 KB), OrderForm_HexaTek_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 64 KB)

From: Sophie Grant <sophie@hexatek.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hexatek.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uplift — redlines and path to sign

Thanks Naomi — reviewing now. A couple immediate clarifications from Procurement:

1) Term: We prefer 12 months (to align with internal budgeting) but are open to 24 months if we can get a 7.5% annual discount and an option to re-evaluate after 12 months. Is that something Redwood can consider?
2) Retention: We will need 12 months for logs for compliance; please send the Exhibit F language and estimate for the incremental cost.
3) SLA credits: procurement wants credits to be automatic (trigger + credit applied to invoice) rather than a credit request process. Is the Exhibit C add-on sufficient?

I’ll get Procurement’s formal response by end of day tomorrow. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Sophie
Head of IT Procurement
HexaTek Inc.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uplift — redlines and path to sign

Naomi / Logan,

Quick internal note before we respond to HexaTek:

- Discount: 7.5% for a 24-month firm term is doable, but we should confirm: is the ask 7.5% off list for both years or year-one only? If it's both years, Legal will want to capture that in the payment schedule.
- SLA credits: I like putting the calculation in Exhibit C and specifying automatic invoice adjustments for creditable incidents. That keeps MSA mechanics intact and gives Procurement the operational behavior they want.
- Retention: Exhibit F language should be limited (explicit retention window, encryption at rest, deletion timeline). We can offer the 12-month retention as an add-on line item on the order form rather than bake into the MSA.

Proposed next steps:
1) Naomi to send a short note to Sophie confirming 12 vs 24 negotiation range and documenting 7.5% trade-off.
2) Attach a short Exhibit F snippet and a proration example for the order form.
3) If Sophie agrees, I’ll prep the final Exhibit C text for automatic SLA credits and copy Legal Ops on the DocuSign packet.

I attached a quick redline summary (snippet pasted below) and the proration table for Ben/Finance — will also add to the HubSpot deal.

-Ben
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

[snippet: Proposed Exhibit C credit calc: Credit = (Downtime minutes/Total SLA minutes) * Monthly fee * 100%; auto-apply to next invoice; credit cap = 100% of monthly fee]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@hexatek.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uplift — redlines and path to sign

Hi Sophie — thanks for the quick reply and for surfacing Procurement priorities. To confirm and make the path-to-sign explicit: 

- Term: Redwood can offer 24 months at a 7.5% annual discount (applies to both years), or a 12-month term at list. If HexaTek needs a 12-month budget cadence, we can do 24 months with an opt-out/re-eval after 12 months documented as an early notice window (we'll propose language).
- Retention: I’m sending the Exhibit F snippet and the estimated line item for 12-month log retention attached. We treat retention as an order-form add-on so the MSA stays standard.
- SLA credits: we'll add an Exhibit C paragraph that makes credit issuance automatic and ties it to the incident traceability in Console; credit will apply to the next invoice and be limited to the monthly fee for the impacted service.

If Procurement accepts the 7.5% for a 24-month term I’ll do the following immediately:
1) Update the order form with the add-on line for retention and the 24-month pricing with discount.
2) Finalize Exhibit C wording and prepare DocuSign.
3) Loop in Legal Ops only on the DocuSign packet — Sophie, if Procurement needs Legal to review redlines, please send counsel contact and we’ll add them to the envelope.

Would you like the revised packet today (EOD) or tomorrow morning?

Best,
Naomi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ExhibitF_retention_snippet.docx (text, 12 KB)

Looping back — quick ops/closing checklist for Naomi: 
- Confirm with Sophie whether the 7.5% applies to both years (Ben will need this for the revenue schedule).
- If Procurement insists on 12-month term only, push for a phased approach in order form (12-month firm with optional extension language) rather than altering MSA term language. Keeps legal churn lower.
- Once Sophie confirms, create the HubSpot deal note and tag Legal Ops with the DocuSign envelope id. I added the HubSpot link below.

I'll be on standby to approve the final Exhibit C wording. Good work moving this quickly — if Procurement wants counsel contact, ask them to send email and we’ll add counsel to the envelope rather than CCing on redlines.
